Tonight and Tuesday: Low pressure remains over the NW U.S., 
with the primary center over Montana and a secondary low over 
the Cascades this afternoon. This will be the primary 
precipitation producer this period. A deformation axis joining 
these feature is providing a focal point for moisture and 
precipitation. The low near the Cascades pivots south and east 
tonight into early Tuesday, which will pivot that boundary  
and that moisture south and east while the precipitation start 
to wane from the west. There could be some embedded t-storms 
this evening, but the risk is expected to past sunset. The 
steadier showers this afternoon were found near the northern 
counties and this will expand south and east. The east third of 
WA and ID will see the best potential for measurable 
precipitation, with more isolated to scattered activity near the
Cascades, central and southeast WA. By Tuesday morning the 
primary potential remains over Idaho and the east third of WA. 
For tonight and Tuesday AM, I did draw the PoPs further west and
south than the NBM was showing as it has been under-performing 
when it comes to the convective showers the past few days. 

By Tuesday afternoon the low is moving east and mainly isolated
showers are forecast around the ID Panhandle mountains. I went 
a bit above guidance here too in the northwest flow, but for the
most part it will be drier. Rain amounts of 0.05 to 0.25 inches
possible over northeast WA and the north and central Panhandle,
locally up to 0.50 in some of the rising terrain over Idaho 
from tonight to early Tuesday. The remainder of central and 
southeast WA and lower ID is generally expected to see less than
0.05 inches of rain, if any.

Breezy conditions will subside through this evening, becoming 
light and variable overnight into Tuesday morning. Lows will be 
in the 40s to low 50s. Highs will be in the upper 60s to 70s 
Tuesday. With the recent rain and high pressure starting to nose
in, look for some patchy to areas of fog over the northeast WA 
and ID Panhandle valleys, as well as sine some outlying areas of
the Palouse and sheltered areas around the Spokane area later 
tonight and again Tuesday night into Wednesday AM.

Wednesday and Thursday: Weak high pressure builds in with a 
drier west to northwest flow, while another system starts to 
drop toward. Skies will be partly to mostly cloudy, with the 
most cloud cover Wednesday night/early Thursday. Look for drier 
weather, with warming temperatures. Highs are forecast to be in 
the 70s to mid-80s, with lows mainly in the 40s and 50s. Winds 
will be on the increase from the north Wednesday night, 
especially down the Okanogan Valley. The broader breezy to windy
conditions are forecast Thursday with a strong westerly flow 
and jet sagging across the region. Speeds of 10-20 mph with 
gusts of 20-25 mph are forecast, with localized gusts near 30 
mph around the Waterville Plateau through western Columbia 
Basin. Elevated fire conditions, blowing dust and choppy waters 
will be something we will keep an eye toward. 

Thursday night to Monday: The next low pressure system drops 
into the region. A weak wave moves across Thursday night into 
Friday, then a stronger low digs down the coast Friday night 
into early Saturday before swinging inland Saturday afternoon 
into Sunday. A few showers are possible around the mountains 
with the first wave, but better chances expand out Friday night 
into Saturday, before starting to retreat to the mountains and 
wane Sunday into Monday. Some moderate rains are possible around
the mountain zones Saturday, with lighter amounts elsewhere. 
Embedded t-storms are possible and may produce locally higher 
amounts. Saturday is also forecast to be another breezy day. 
Temperatures cool to the mid-60s and 70s Friday, mostly 60s and 
localized low 70s Saturday, before moderating into Sunday and 
Monday. Lows will be mainly in the 50s, but We will have to 
watch for some mid to upper 30s in some of the sheltered valleys
and outlying areas over east WA and ID. /Solveig
